title: EXACT CHANGE, a ps1-style night shift game I've been building with Claude code (first trailer, shot in-engine)
author: sowcow9
selftext:
I've had this idea for a long time and finally got around to building it this week thanks to claude code. 

You run a vending route at night while the town's asleep, restocking machines at a laundromat, a bowling alley, a motel and a truck stop. ps1 style, made in godot.

Everything in the trailer was shot in-engine. claude wrote a camera mode that glides between poses and triggers the real game stuff, like rolling the ball or pulling a tray. that chase down the bowling lane took a few tries. At first the camera was a solid object, so when following the ball, it kept nudging it into the gutter. so, I had to make the camera a *ghost*. the cart rolling through the depot door was a fight too, it kept jamming because only half of the double door opens. 

Before every shot claude sketches the room from above with a few camera paths along with storyboards, a surprising addition and extremely helpful.

From there it built me a capcut project with every shot on its own track, and I did the final cut.

I'd love to hear what people think! **Is there anything in the trailer that dragged or felt off?**  
And **what's the weirdest place you've ever seen a vending machine?** looking for my next stop.

comments.author: MaleficentClub7480
comments.body: Very nice! Mind sharing your art workflow? Blender?  Any special prompt? Reference images? :) Ty!

replies.author: sowcow9
replies.body:
thanks! yeah, blender. claude drives the live blender through an MCP addon while I watch the viewport and tell it what’s off. at first it built models blind from scripted shapes and they never matched, so now everything gets shaped where I can see it. the people and the hands start from free CC0 ps1 packs.

the snack packaging started as AI images from Flow (all made up brands). the rest is CC0 photo textures or stuff drawn in code with real fonts. then one python script crunches all of it the ps1 way, tiny textures with a tiny palette, and godot snaps everything to 320x240 with dither and fog.

no special prompt really, just a list of rules that keeps growing every time something looks off.
